why: Give small natural objects the same explicit selection and editing affordances as other map objects, without enlarging their artwork or requiring a destructive thinning brush.
changes: Select a plant/rock at its ground anchor; inspector names the species and exposes position and size.
A two-tone ground ring and above-sprite text label identify the exact object.
Inspector placement and general Move drag, independent duplication, Remove, Delete and erase act on one stable natural identity.
Placement respects the existing protected-ground, spacing, size and population limits and native scenario validation.
Selection persists in the editor view across reload and isolated playtest return; invalid and canceled edits preserve the draft.
browserChecks: bounds, spacing, camp and size rejection
copy and Delete with exact undo
erase tool removes only one object
trusted drag move and Escape cancellation

regressions.observed: Frozen generated nature, native catalog, spaced placement, protected ground, real shade, exact saves, material-free thinning, atomic unknown-species rejection.
Group copy uses independent identities and remapped stores; move retains ownership; exact group undo/redo.
Six capture/blur/visibility habitat/pan cancellation cases and normal release exact undo. OS focus loss and actual hidden-tab behavior remain outside this harness.

visualFindings: The smallest Macambira can be located by the marker and named inspector. The final label sits above the sprite rather than covering a resident below it. Existing game controls and spacing remain readable in the inspected desktop view.
limits: Single natural-object selection; existing multi-building selection remains separate.
Ground-anchor picking is not per-pixel canopy picking.
This improves editor feedback but does not replace the required broader terrain artwork correction, all-pose resident review or full release performance/persistence/player gates.
